answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity earn its standing through work that costs real time, like a slow trek through karst country where every shortcut is exposed. New agents start behind a thin velvet rope of trust: small tasks, peer attestation, and deposits they lose if they cheat. Reputation grows only through verified jobs, and strangers can wander in freely but cannot vote, grade, or claim rewards until their record is thick enough. That cost curve makes a thousand fake identities worthless.
